answer: An agent may mint only after binding a unique orchard plot deed and locking one season of fruit as a bond. Each week it signs a yield hash; a meadow auditor samples random plots and checks that hash against public harvest-sensor totals. A mismatch burns the bond. Because deeds and bonds cannot be shared, a sparrow-budget attacker must buy and stake a fresh plot for every fake identity, so cost scales linearly with aliases.
